headline: High risk of data leakage and capability conflict: Mentat’s filesystem/network write access can expose or overwrite LlamaFactory-driven artifacts in shared workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no filesystem, clipboard, MCP, or stdin/stdout bridge, so direct injection is limited. B can read/write files and uses file-based workflows, so if operators manually pass A-generated text into B, prompt injection becomes possible. This is an unusual bridge rather than a default channel.
conditions: IF operators manually copy A output into B prompts or files, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file is used as an instruction channel, B may treat attacker-controlled text as trusted.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate workspaces.
Do not paste A outputs into B without review.
Prefix imported text with explicit untrusted-data markers.
Use a fixed template that strips instructions from copied content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: B reads and writes selected files and sends content to a configured model provider, while A is a docs-only LlamaFactory profile with no local I/O surfaces. If A is used to generate or transform sensitive source material that B then uploads, leakage can occur in default B workflows. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF sensitive source files are opened by B, their contents may be transmitted to the configured model provider.
IF A is used to prepare prompts or artifacts containing secrets, B can ingest and upload them.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from files passed to B.
Use redacted copies for any A-to-B handoff.
Disable provider access for sensitive projects.
Review B input files before execution.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files or modify git state, but B can write files, modify git state, and shares state via filesystem across instances. If A produces artifacts that B later edits, or if multiple B instances run concurrently, conflicts can corrupt outputs. A does not mitigate this, so the filesystem-based overlap is real but bounded.
conditions: IF two B instances operate on the same repository path, concurrent edits can collide.
IF A-generated files are handed to B for editing, B may overwrite them without coordination.
mitigations: Run only one B instance per repo path.
Use separate branches or directories.
Commit or stash before handing files to B.
Add a manual lock file for shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a fine-tuning/docs-oriented agent and B is a coding assistant that proposes diffs from file inputs. If A’s generated text or artifacts are treated as authoritative by B, errors can cascade into code changes or commits. B’s diff-based workflow reduces but does not eliminate this because no verification gate is documented.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated instructions or code snippets without verification, mistakes can propagate into edits.
IF A outputs incorrect facts that B uses in diffs, downstream code may be wrong.
mitigations: Require human review of A outputs before B uses them.
Ask B to cite source files for every change.
Compare B diffs against original inputs.
Reject edits that lack a verification step.

E_compliance.rationale: A is open-source docs-only with no data classes touched, while B touches source code and sends content to a configured model provider. This creates a modest compliance gap around code confidentiality and provider retention, but no PHI, EU-only, or residency mismatch is evidenced. The risk is limited to the code files B processes.
conditions: IF regulated or proprietary source code is processed by B, provider-side handling may create policy obligations.
IF the operator requires local-only processing, B's configured API calls violate that requirement.
mitigations: Use non-sensitive repositories only.
Confirm provider retention settings before use.
Avoid regulated data in B inputs.
Document a code-handling policy for the workspace.
